summary: redis1 is the only node in the cluster with a memory cap and an eviction policy (maxmemory 5 MB + allkeys-lru, vs maxmemory 0 + noeviction on redis2 and redis3), so it sits permanently at its cap and LRU-evicts roughly its entire ~67k-key share down to ~525 keys - destroying the dedup and velocity state for the one-third of the keyspace hashing to its slots, which makes fraud detection silently under-count with no errors raised.
reasoning: Confirmed via read_config across all three nodes showing the config asymmetry (redis1: maxmemory=5242880/allkeys-lru; redis2/redis3: maxmemory=0/noeviction), independently corroborated by Redis RDB persistence logs showing a ~128x key-count imbalance (redis1: 525 keys/211KB vs redis2: 67005 keys/15.1MB vs redis3: 67777 keys/15.2MB), plus Prometheus showing memory pinned at the 5MB cap and a 313,329-eviction vs 7,980-expiration ratio (keys dying by LRU long before TTL). Explicitly anchored to the list_recent_changes injection timestamp (20:56:38Z) and ruled out an earlier redis2 restart/CLUSTERDOWN episode as a prior, already-resolved incident rather than the current fault. Two caveats noted: the exporter only scrapes redis1 so historical drift timing is circumstantial (though strongly time-correlated), and redis2/redis3 are separately growing unbounded under noeviction, a latent second risk.
